processes.label: Sign in
processes.title: A workstation finds its identity.
processes.caption: Addressing, name resolution, and domain authentication.

steps.title: Obtain a network address
steps.description: A new client requests an address and receives lease settings. The exchange includes discovery, offer, request, and acknowledgement.

steps.title: Locate directory services
steps.description: The workstation asks internal DNS to locate domain services. DNS records connect service names to reachable hosts.

steps.title: Authenticate to the domain
steps.description: The client proves its identity to the domain controller’s Key Distribution Center and obtains a ticket-granting ticket.

steps.title: Read directory information
steps.description: Directory clients retrieve the information they need from Active Directory. Protection and binding behavior depend on the client and server configuration.

processes.label: Open a file
processes.title: From a name to an authorized file.
processes.caption: Follow a domain client to its file share.

steps.title: Resolve the file server
steps.description: The client resolves the file server’s name before opening a connection. The diagram uses SBD-FS01 as the named destination.

steps.title: Request a service ticket
steps.description: The workstation uses its ticket-granting ticket to request a ticket for the file service. It then presents that service ticket to the server.

steps.title: Open the approved share
steps.description: The client requests a file over SMB. The server applies the relevant share and filesystem permissions before allowing access.

processes.label: Get updates
processes.title: Bring updates inside. Distribute with care.
processes.caption: A disconnected update workflow, with no internet edge.

steps.title: Import approved update material
steps.description: An authorized operator brings approved update material across the air gap using controlled media and an established import process.

steps.title: Check update metadata
steps.description: The client contacts the internal WSUS service for update metadata using the TLS-enabled configuration.

steps.title: Retrieve signed update content
steps.description: WSUS uses its HTTP connection for update payloads, with signatures protecting payload authenticity. TLS is used for metadata rather than every WSUS path.

processes.label: Follow a log
processes.title: Turn an event into useful evidence.
processes.caption: From a Linux source to collection, analysis, and retention.

steps.title: Deliver a source event
steps.description: A configured Linux source can initiate a protected syslog session to the collector. The connection uses TLS transport.

steps.title: Ingest for investigation
steps.description: The collection layer supplies events to Splunk for indexing and investigation. The exact forwarder, API, or input method must be chosen.

steps.title: Retain an audit copy
steps.description: An approved archive process preserves the records needed for review and retention. This is a proposed collector-to-repository relationship.

processes.label: License check
processes.title: A licensing service has its own contract.
processes.caption: Follow the client request to its licensing service.

steps.title: Request a license
steps.description: An approved client contacts the licensing service to check or obtain its entitlement. Protocol, direction, persistence, and offline behavior depend on the product.

processes.label: Offline trust
processes.title: The root stays outside the live network.
processes.caption: A controlled offline certificate ceremony.

steps.title: Prepare the signing material
steps.description: Prepare the subordinate CA’s signing request and the records required for the ceremony. Protect the request and validate the intended certificate policy.

steps.title: Use the offline root
steps.description: Authorized operators use the protected root key in a controlled ceremony. The root CA remains non-domain-joined and disconnected.

steps.title: Return publication artifacts
steps.description: Return approved certificate and revocation artifacts through the documented offline transfer process. Define the issuing CA’s enrollment and publication design separately.

processes.label: Use a web app
processes.title: A browser trusts the internal web service.
processes.caption: Name resolution, certificate trust, and an encrypted session.

steps.title: Resolve the web server
steps.description: The browser resolves the web service’s internal name before connecting. DNS returns SBD-WEB01’s address on VLAN 40.

steps.title: Verify the server certificate
steps.description: The browser opens a TLS session. SBD-WEB01 presents a certificate from the internal issuing CA, and the client checks the name, validity dates, and chain to the trusted offline root.

steps.title: Request the application
steps.description: Inside the encrypted session, the browser sends HTTP requests and receives the application’s responses. The application decides what the signed-in user may see.

whatIfs.label: DC01 is down
whatIfs.title: One domain controller fails.
whatIfs.caption: The client turns to SBD-DC02 for DNS and authentication.

steps.title: Query SBD-DC01
steps.description: The workstation sends its DNS query to its first configured DNS server. SBD-DC01 is offline, so no reply comes back.

steps.title: Retry with SBD-DC02
steps.description: The client retries with its next configured DNS server. SBD-DC02 also provides DNS for the domain and answers.

steps.title: Authenticate with SBD-DC02
steps.description: DNS service records list both domain controllers, and the client’s domain controller locator finds SBD-DC02 responding. SBD-DC02’s Key Distribution Center issues the ticket-granting ticket.

whatIfs.label: Certificate expired
whatIfs.title: The browser refuses an expired certificate.
whatIfs.caption: Trust checks fail before any application data is sent.

steps.title: Resolve the web server
steps.description: The browser resolves the web service’s internal name, exactly as on a normal day.

steps.title: Present an expired certificate
steps.description: SBD-WEB01 presents a certificate whose validity period has ended. The browser checks the dates, stops the connection, and shows a certificate error.

whatIfs.label: A PC tries SQL
whatIfs.title: Default deny stops a direct database connection.
whatIfs.caption: No exception exists for workstation-to-SQL traffic.

steps.title: Connect straight to SBD-SQL01
steps.description: A workstation tries to reach the database server directly. The core finds no matching exception, so default deny drops the session.

whatIfs.label: PC-to-PC remote desktop
whatIfs.title: Host firewalls stop lateral movement.
whatIfs.caption: One workstation tries remote desktop to another.

steps.title: Open remote desktop to another PC
steps.description: A workstation tries a remote desktop session to a peer on the same VLAN. The destination’s host firewall refuses it.

whatIfs.label: Attack drill
whatIfs.title: An intruder tests every boundary.
whatIfs.caption: Six moves an intruder might try, from one compromised PC to a stolen admin session. Each is checked against the rules.

steps.title: A compromised PC tries the database
steps.description: Malware on one workstation reaches straight for SBD-SQL01. No exception exists for workstation-to-SQL traffic, so the core drops the attempt.
steps.test: Client-to-SQL, client-to-management, and peer SMB/RDP fail.

steps.title: It looks for the security tools
steps.description: Taking over a security tool would blind the defenders. The PC tries Splunk’s web interface. No rule lets user workstations reach security-tool management, so default deny drops it.
steps.test: A compromised client cannot reach security-tool management interfaces.

steps.title: It tries a neighbour’s file shares
steps.description: Next, the PC tries the shares on another workstation in VLAN 80. The traffic never crosses the core, so the neighbour’s host firewall refuses it.
steps.test: Client-to-SQL, client-to-management, and peer SMB/RDP fail.

steps.title: It tries remote desktop to a neighbour
steps.description: The PC tries a remote desktop session to a peer. The destination’s host firewall refuses it.
steps.test: Client-to-SQL, client-to-management, and peer SMB/RDP fail.

steps.title: A compromised web server reaches for the database
steps.description: If SBD-WEB01 were taken over, SBD-SQL01 would be the next target. They share VLAN 40, so the core never sees this traffic. SBD-SQL01’s host firewall keeps it blocked.
steps.test: The web server cannot access SQL before an approved dependency exists.

steps.title: A stolen admin session aims at a domain controller
steps.description: With an endpoint administrator’s stolen session on SBD-ADMIN-PC01, the attacker aims at SBD-DC01. That host manages user endpoints only. No rule lets it manage a domain controller, so default deny drops it.
steps.test: An endpoint administrator cannot manage a DC, issuing CA, or member server.
